name: Matutinal-Bajada
description: Rolling continents break around shallow seas, their interiors scored by tectonic rift valleys. Beyond towering mountain ranges, the land runs to a horizon that feels hand-drawn.

The air carries ozone and crushed stone, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Herds of six-limbed graziers shadow the meltwater margins, wary of anything that walks upright.
Core samples from the deep crust contain isotopes with no known decay chain. The samples are stored off-world now, and studied reluctantly.

For traders, biomass, platinum, iron and solar potential alone justifies the crossing; for everyone else, the planet pays in questions. Fuel is cheap, information is not, and both are dangerous to carry.
